steps.why: The phenotype is what an observer records, which is why it is the only thing Mendel could count directly.
common_mistakes: Saying the phenotype is the gene. That is the GENOTYPE.
Giving no example. One word is enough and it fixes the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Phenotype is what you can see.

steps.margin_note: Definition, examples, and the TT-versus-Tt point that links the two.

TT and Tt have the SAME phenotype (tall) but
DIFFERENT genotypes, which is why a test cross

steps.why: One phenotype can come from more than one genotype, and that gap between the two is the reason genetics needs both words.
common_mistakes: Saying every genotype has its own phenotype. TT and Tt look identical.
Giving no letters. The letter examples are what make the two terms concrete.
steps.memory_tip: Genotype is what you carry; phenotype is what shows.
